Case 9's numbers checked by hand against the sources. ISO 273: I fetched the iTeh preview PDF the repo cites (https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/4183/.../ISO-273-1979.pdf), rendered page 2 of the standard and read the table: M8 is fine 8.4, medium 9, coarse 10 (M6 6.4/6.6/7, M10 10.5/11/12 also match CLEARANCE). EN 1993-1-8 Table 3.3: a search returned the text of a BS EN 1993-1-8:2005 copy (phd.eng.br PDF) and two summaries giving minimum e1 = 1.2 d0, e2 = 1.2 d0, p1 = 2.2 d0, p2 = 2.4 d0 (maximum e1 4t + 40 mm), matching BOLT_SPACING. I read these as snippets, not as the table image. Arithmetic: d0 = 9.0, 1.2 d0 = 10.8; 40 mm bore: 20 + 10.8 = 30.8; 50 mm bore: 25 + 10.8 = 35.8; both match case 9 and the test's output. Six holes at 30.8 mm are 30.8 mm apart (2 r sin 30 deg), over 2.2 d0 = 19.8, and the flange's 80 mm radius leaves 49.2 mm to its edge, over 10.8, so the imprint checks do not refuse. Bolt: grip 10 + 6 = 16, two ISO 7089 M8 washers 1.6 each = 3.2, ISO 4032 M8 nut 6.8, two pitches of 1.25 = 2.5, total 28.5 mm; the shortest ISO 4017 M8 length at or above it is 30 (28 falls short), so 'bolt M8x30' as case 8 works it. The washer, nut and pitch figures are from my knowledge of the standards, not re-fetched (the Firecrawl account was out of credits).

Read the run log. The test builds its own log: the ids of the nodes whose run count rose, in engine order, with each node's `says`. The app's own run log (view/nodes.ts lastRan, view/dashboard.ts logRun) lists nodes that ran anew by `label`, in sequence order, with milliseconds and no `says` text. placeBlock sets label to the block's name, so on a board made the way the test makes it the app log would show 'Imprint a pattern' twice. The test's names come from the ids the test gives the nodes. Noted, not held against the check, which says 'the run log names each step' and whose case lists those ids.

Noted limit: the 'bore' is a number node feeding relation.boltcircle. The flange is a plain cylinder with no bore cut in it, so widening the bore moves the bolt circle, the six holes in each plate and the bolts, but no solid changes shape at the bore. Case 9's own `ran` list treats the bore as a node and the check's words ask for the bolt circle, bolts and cover's holes to follow, so this is not a miss. The bolts are a text and a table of positions, not placed bolt parts; also outside the check's words.
